extra.explanation_full: Explanation: What’s causing this unusually long cloud on Mars ? Known as the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC) and first recorded by NASA’s Viking Orbiter 2 in 1977, the strange cloud has been imaged in greater detail more recently by ESA ’s robotic Mars Express spacecraft. The featured image is from 2018. The cloud forms only during spring and summer seasons and then only during morning hours. Made of water-ice, the most familiar process that causes cloud crystals to form around bits of dust would fail due to the thinness and lack of dust high in the Martian atmosphere . Leading speculation holds that dust is not involved. After the cloud forms near the volcano Arsia Mons , wind blows the cloud downstream — creating a tail that can extend over 1500 kilometers. Efforts to better understand AMEC s will continue, an understanding that may bolster a more complete view of cloud formation on Earth . Tomorrow's picture: eyeing a cat

extra.alt: Mars is seen from orbit with an orange landscape and two prominent volcanoes on the right. Extending  horizontally from the nearer volcano is a very long white cloud.

items.commentary: 2026-11-02 的每日天文图《A Long Cloud on Mars》。今日看构图：先别看主体，找画面里最重的那一块，看它把视线推向哪里。
《Overseer Shabti of Nauny》：Faience、Third Intermediate Period、ca. 1051–1002 BCE。今日看构图：眯起眼只看大轮廓，数数留白占了多大、又留给了谁。
